item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlights | The Hapless Helper
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

SCP becomes pale and sickly if it cannot provide aid to others.

I'm a little hesitant about this, and this kind of thing in general: it's usually less interesting to me if you add anomalous properties to a SCP that force the Foundation to let it do things than if you have a good narrative reason for the Foundation to let it do things, y'know?

After intense review, the SCP was allowed to accompany scientists and help within the site it is located at.

I'm kinda hesitant about this because a large part of the idea here is that the SCP tries to be helpful and isn't?

I want to keep the focus of the article on the mysteries surrounding the SCP and its desire to connect with members of the Foundation.

What is this mystery? This feels like the it's meant to be the core of the article but it also don't particularly feel like something interesting to explore; but I don't really know how you're like…intending exploring this? Like, how are you setting this mystery up to the reader? How are you getting the reader invested in it's outcome? How are you resolving the mystery?

My concern is that it feels like the most interesting part of this is the bit between the SCP Allison joining the foundation and them discovering the Thumbling, and the thumbling growing into becoming an actually valuable member of the Foundation, and like, the story of their growth; and it feels like you've not really…covered that section at all?

item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlights | The Hapless Helper
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the critique!

+ Read More
- Read Less

I think you worded it fine, it didn't feel harsh. I definitely can see your issues with it. The section relating to the O5 was one aspect I wasn't certain about keeping in the concept. I'd be fine with scrapping the O5 aspect.

Containing him should be the priority regardless of if he knows anyone in the Foundation. My only reason for saying the SCP should help was due to his survival basically requiring him to help others.

The closeness to the thumbling is also a pretty big issue which I'm unsure of how I should tackle.

item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlights | The Hapless Helper
item.content:encoded:
Hey, there. Let's take a look, shall we?

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

This feels like an alternate take of the story of the Thumbling with an SCP subplot slapped on to remind the reader that this takes place in the Foundationverse. There's nothing wrong with taking inspiration from old fairy tales, but, coming from someone who read Thumbling, I think this hits way too close to home for its own good.

Also, befriending a girl who would later grow up to be O5 is…kinda convenient. Kinda extremely convenient. Possible? I suppose. Plausible? Probably not.

Even if we got over the convenience of this Thumbling befriending a future O5, I fully believe they'd still contain him. The Foundation exists to contain. Even if the O5 girl was friends with him pre-containment, as cold as it sounds, she'd most definitely put this dangerous and highly prestigious job over her old friend. She'd have to if she wanted to keep her job.

Even if she did break protocol, there are 12 other O5 Council members who would most definitely outvote her.

I absolutely do not buy them letting this random thumb-sized man help out around the Foundation. They have personnel.

Honestly…I don't know what advice to offer. This is too close to an actual existing fairytale, I feel like. I'm not sure how to improve this and I'm always hesitant to tell someone to scrap an idea.

I suggest reaching out to someone on the butterfly squad roster and trying to get a second opinion.

Anywho, I apologise if this was harsh, but I do hope I helped! 👍

Have a good one!

item.title: Looking for Greenlights | The Hapless Helper
item.content:encoded:
The Hapless Helper
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional/Mystery

Elevator Pitch:
Based on the Thumbling (Grimm Fairytale)
- A tiny man the size of a thumb that seeks to help others.
- It can inadvertently hinder those it tries to help.
- SCP becomes pale and sickly if it cannot provide aid to others.

Central Narrative:

- SCP first appeared to keep a peasant family company.
- It travelled the world, aiming to help, typically causing harm, but being legitimately helpful on several occasions.

+ show block
– hide block

- An example of a hindrance was when the SCP aiming to ‘help’ robbers burgling a cottage. It loudly performed the actions it was told, waking the residents.
- The SCP left, assuming it helped the family when in actuality, it ended up causing the family to be shot after they tried confronting the robbers.

- Appeared and kept in contact with a girl it calls Allison who would later become a worker in the SCP Foundation, who joined in order to find the Thumbling once more.
- After intense review, the SCP was allowed to accompany scientists and help within the site it is located at.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Concise article with an interview log to explain the SCP’s connection to Alison.

Additional Notes: I want to keep the focus of the article on the mysteries surrounding the SCP and its desire to connect with members of the Foundation. I generally want the article to feel like the SCP is a positive influence but with a slight hint of dread that something may go wrong in the future.

(I edited the mention of Alison being an O5 member to her being a regular worker in the SCP Foundation)


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
